statement_record.book: A discrete dynamical system is a set X with an endomorphism f : X -> X and a point x0 ∈ X. (N, s, 0) is the universal such system: for every (X, f, x0) there is a UNIQUE r : N -> X with r·0 = x0 and r ∘ s = f ∘ r; i.e. (N, s, 0) is the initial object of the category of discrete dynamical systems.
statement_record.intree: cata_commutes : cata β ∘ inα ≈ β ∘ fmap[F] (cata β)  together with  cata_unique : (h ∘ inα ≈ β ∘ fmap[F] h) → h ≈ cata β — the existence-and-uniqueness of the mediating map out of an initial F-algebra, for an arbitrary endofunctor F and an ASSUMED Initial (FAlg F).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the recursion principle is proven only parametrically, as a conditional over an assumed initial object of FAlg F. statement_record.book: (i) c is initial in C iff the covariant hom-functor C(c,-) : C -> Set is naturally isomorphic to the constant functor at the one-point set; (ii) c is terminal iff C(-,c) : C^op -> Set is naturally isomorphic to the corresponding constant singleton functor. Equivalently C has an initial (resp. terminal) object exactly when the constant singleton functor on C (resp. on C^op) is representable.

statement_record.book: For a Set-valued functor F on a LOCALLY SMALL category C: (i) a representation of F is an object c together with a specified natural isomorphism α : C(c,-) ⇒ F (covariant) or α : C(-,c) ⇒ F (contravariant); one says c represents F. (ii) F is representable if such data exists. A representation encodes a universal property of c: covariant representations describe arrows out of c, contravariant ones arrows into c.
statement_record.intree: Class Representable `(F : C ⟶ Sets) := { repr_obj : C; represented : [Hom repr_obj,─] ≅ F }, together with representability_by_yoneda for the contravariant form (Isomorphism [Hom ─,c] F ≅ the universal elements of F c) and univ_property_unique_up_to_unique_iso for the encoded universal property.

statement_record.book: Seven contravariant Set-valued functors with representing objects: (i) the power set functor P : Set^op -> Set is represented by 2 via characteristic functions, naturality being 'precompose = take preimage'; (ii) the open-set functor on Top^op is represented by the Sierpinski space; (iii) the closed-set functor is also represented by it, so O ≅ C via complementation; (iv) X ↦ {functions X × A -> B} is represented by B^A — this natural iso is currying; (v) the dual-vector-space functor is represented by the ground field; (vi) singular cohomology H^n(-;A) on CW homotopy classes is represented by K(A,n); (vii) principal G-bundles are represented by BG.

statement_record.strength_comparison: mixed. Clause (iv) is same-or-stronger: exp_iso is stated for any cartesian closed category (not just Set), it is an iso of hom-setoids, and curry_comp_l supplies the naturality. Clause (i) is intree-weaker in one precise respect: classifier_classifies is a PER-OBJECT isomorphism of setoids, not a natural isomorphism Sub ≅ [Hom ─,Ω] of presheaves, even though the presheaf Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets exists (Theory/Subobject/Functor.v:180) — so the book's naturality clause ('precomposing a classifying map with f computes the preimage', i.e. char (f* m) ≈ char m ∘ f) is never asserted, and 'representable' is never claimed. Clauses (ii),(iii),(v),(vi),(vii) have no in-tree counterpart at all.
